findings.title: L’AFP coupe l’accès à sa plateforme après une cyberattaque
findings.summary_md: Clubic published the first account of the incident on 26 November 2026, reporting that Agence France-Presse closed AFP Forum, the client portal for downloading dispatches and images, after an intrusion during the night of Wednesday to Thursday. Citing an internal management message reported by Le Monde, it states the attackers struck from 01:30 Paris time and that AFP isolated the platform as soon as the intrusion was detected, with analyses continuing under external experts and no identification of the attackers. It also records the earlier September 2024 attack on part of AFP's content delivery systems and notes that French authorities have counted an average of three data thefts per day in the country since January.

findings.title: L’Agence France-Presse dit avoir été visée par une cyberattaque qui paralyse l’une de ses plateformes de mise à disposition des dépêches et des images
findings.summary_md: Le Monde reported on 26 November 2026 that AFP said it had been targeted by a cyberattack that paralysed one of its platforms for providing dispatches and images to clients. The article carried AFP's statement on Thursday evening that it had no information on the identity of the attackers, and it is the source other French outlets credit for the internal management message describing the 01:30 Paris detection.

findings.title: Agence France-Presse says cyberattack targeted IT systems
findings.summary_md: The Record reported on 30 September 2024 that AFP said hackers attacked its IT systems the preceding Friday, affecting part of its delivery service to clients. AFP said the perpetrators were unknown and that its technical teams were working with the French national agency ANSSI, with the relevant authorities notified, while its newsroom continued normal coverage. No group claimed the incident and AFP did not answer questions on whether it faced ransomware, the report adding that AFP was founded in 1835 and operates in 150 countries.
